@staticmethod
    def _partitioned_sublattice_groups(ordered_constituents, disordered_constituents):
        """
        Return the ordered sublattices corresponding to each disordered sublattice.

        In a partitioned (order-disorder) model, the ordered phase description
        splits sublattices of the disordered description into several
        symmetry-distinct position classes of the same physical lattice. Every
        sublattice of the disordered description therefore corresponds to a
        group of one or more sublattices of the ordered description. Sublattices
        that are not split by the ordered description (e.g. interstitial or
        vacancy-only sublattices) correspond to a group of exactly one ordered
        sublattice, and their occupancies are unaffected by ordering.

        Following the convention of thermodynamic databases (and of the site
        ratios declared by both descriptions), the sublattices created by the
        ordering split are the leading sublattices of the ordered description,
        while the trailing sublattices correspond one-to-one to the trailing
        sublattices of the disordered description.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ordered_constituents : list of list of Species
            Constituents of every sublattice of the ordered description.
        disordered_constituents : list of list of Species
            Constituents of every sublattice of the disordered description.

        Returns
        -------
        list of tuple of int
            For each sublattice of the disordered description, the indices of
            the corresponding sublattices of the ordered description.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> # (AL,FE)(AL,FE)(AL,FE)(AL,FE)(VA) ordering of (AL,FE)(VA)
        >>> Model._partitioned_sublattice_groups([['AL', 'FE']]*4 + [['VA']], [['AL', 'FE'], ['VA']])
        [(0, 1, 2, 3), (4,)]
        """
        num_ordered_subl = len(ordered_constituents)
        num_disordered_subl = len(disordered_constituents)
        if num_disordered_subl > num_ordered_subl:
            raise DofError(
                'The disordered description ({0} sublattices) cannot have more '
                'sublattices than the ordered description ({1} sublattices) of '
                'a partitioned model'.format(num_disordered_subl, num_ordered_subl))
        # Number of ordered position classes that partition the first
        # sublattice of the disordered description
        num_partitioned_subl = num_ordered_subl - num_disordered_subl + 1
        subl_groups = [tuple(range(num_partitioned_subl))]
        subl_groups.extend((num_partitioned_subl + idx,) for idx in range(num_disordered_subl - 1))
        return subl_groups

    @staticmethod
    def _disordered_site_fraction(species, phase_name, sublattice_group,
                                  constituent_array, site_ratios):
        """
        Return the occupancy of a species on a group of ordered sublattices when
        the group is in the disordered state.

        The disordered occupancy of a physical lattice is the average of the
        occupancies of its ordered position classes, weighted by the site ratios
        of those classes. A group containing a single sublattice is not
        partitioned by the ordered description, so its site fraction is returned
        unchanged.

        Parameters
        ----------
        species : Species
            Species to compute the disordered occupancy of.
        phase_name : str
            Name of the ordered phase.
        sublattice_group : Iterable of int
            Indices of the ordered sublattices belonging to one physical
            lattice, i.e. one sublattice of the disordered description.
        constituent_array : list of list of Species
            Active constituents of every sublattice of the ordered description.
        site_ratios : Iterable
            Site ratios of every sublattice of the ordered description.

        Returns
        -------
        SymPy object
        """
        sublattice_group = tuple(sublattice_group)
        if len(sublattice_group) == 1:
            # This lattice is not partitioned by the ordered description, so
            # ordering does not change its occupancy.
            subl_index = sublattice_group[0]
            if species in constituent_array[subl_index]:
                return v.SiteFraction(phase_name, subl_index, species)
            # The species does not exist on this lattice in the ordered
            # description, so its occupancy is zero.
            return S.Zero
        site_ratio_normalization = sum(site_ratios[idx] for idx in sublattice_group)
        numerator = Add(*[site_ratios[idx] * v.SiteFraction(phase_name, idx, species)
                          for idx in sublattice_group if species in constituent_array[idx]])
        return numerator / site_ratio_normalization

    def atomic_ordering_energy(self, dbe):
        """
        Return the atomic ordering contribution in symbolic form.
        Description follows Servant and Ansara, Calphad, 2001.

        Notes
        -----
        The energy of a partitioned model is the energy of the disordered
        description, evaluated at the disordered occupancies implied by the
        ordered internal degrees of freedom, plus the ordering energy

        .. math:: G^{ord}(y) - G^{ord}(y = x)

        which vanishes when the ordered position classes of every physical
        lattice are equally occupied. Both terms require the mapping between
        the sublattices of the two descriptions, which is a structural property
        of the phase descriptions; see `Model._partitioned_sublattice_groups`
        and `Model._disordered_site_fraction`. In particular, sublattices which
        are not created by the ordering split (such as interstitial sublattices,
        with or without vacancies) map one-to-one onto the corresponding
        sublattice of the disordered description and must not be aggregated with
        the occupancies of the partitioned lattice, even when they share a
        species (e.g. vacancies) with it.
        """
        phase = dbe.phases[self.phase_name]
        ordered_phase_name = phase.model_hints.get('ordered_phase', None)
        disordered_phase_name = phase.model_hints.get('disordered_phase', None)
        if phase.name != ordered_phase_name:
            return S.Zero
        disordered_model = self.__class__(dbe, sorted(self.components),
                                          disordered_phase_name)
        ordered_phase = dbe.phases[ordered_phase_name]
        disordered_phase = dbe.phases[disordered_phase_name]
        constituents = [sorted(set(c).intersection(self.components)) \
                for c in ordered_phase.constituents]
        site_ratios = ordered_phase.sublattices
        # Sublattices of the ordered description corresponding to each
        # sublattice of the disordered description
        subl_groups = self._partitioned_sublattice_groups(ordered_phase.constituents,
                                                          disordered_phase.constituents)
        # Reverse mapping: ordered sublattice index -> its group
        group_of_ordered_subl = {}
        for subl_group in subl_groups:
            for subl_index in subl_group:
                group_of_ordered_subl[subl_index] = subl_group

        # Fix variable names
        variable_rename_dict = {}
        disordered_sitefracs = [x for x in disordered_model.energy.free_symbols if isinstance(x, v.SiteFraction)]
        for atom in disordered_sitefracs:
            # Replace the site fractions of the disordered description with the
            # disordered occupancies of the corresponding ordered sublattices.
            variable_rename_dict[atom] = \
                self._disordered_site_fraction(
                    atom.species,
                    ordered_phase_name,
                    subl_groups[atom.sublattice_index],
                    constituents,
                    site_ratios
                    )
        # Save all of the ordered energy contributions
        # This step is why this routine must be called _last_ in build_phase
        ordered_energy = Add(*list(self.models.values()))
        self.models.clear()
        # Copy the disordered energy contributions into the correct bins
        for name, value in disordered_model.models.items():
            self.models[name] = value.xreplace(variable_rename_dict)
        # All magnetic parameters will be defined in the disordered model
        self.TC = self.curie_temperature = disordered_model.TC
        self.TC = self.curie_temperature = self.TC.xreplace(variable_rename_dict)

        molefraction_dict = {}

        # Construct a dictionary that replaces every site fraction with its
        # occupancy in the disordered state
        ordered_sitefracs = [x for x in ordered_energy.free_symbols if isinstance(x, v.SiteFraction)]
        for sitefrac in ordered_sitefracs:
            subl_group = group_of_ordered_subl[sitefrac.sublattice_index]
            if len(subl_group) == 1:
                # Sublattices that are not created by the ordering split are
                # unchanged in the disordered state and should not be replaced.
                # This handles interstitial sublattices, e.g. cases like
                # AL,NI,VA:AL,NI,VA:VA or AL,FE,VA:AL,FE,VA:C,VA, and ensures
                # that species shared with the partitioned lattice (such as
                # vacancies) don't get mixed up.
                continue
            molefraction_dict[sitefrac] = \
                self._disordered_site_fraction(sitefrac.species,
                                               ordered_phase_name, subl_group,
                                               constituents, site_ratios)

        return ordered_energy - ordered_energy.xreplace(molefraction_dict)

def einstein_energy(self, dbe):
        """
        Return the energy based on the Einstein model.
        Note that THETA parameters are actually LN(THETA).
        All Redlich-Kister summation is done in log-space,
        then exp() is called on the result.
        """
        phase = dbe.phases[self.phase_name]
        param_search = dbe.search
        theta_param_query = (
            (where('phase_name') == phase.name) & \
            (where('parameter_type') == 'THETA') & \
            (where('constituent_array').test(self._array_validity))
        )
        lntheta = self.redlich_kister_sum(phase, param_search, theta_param_query)
        theta = exp(lntheta)
        if lntheta != 0:
            result = 1.5*v.R*theta + 3*v.R*v.T*log(1-exp(-theta/v.T))
        else:
            result = 0
        return result / self._site_ratio_normalization

    @staticmethod
    def mole_fraction(species_name, phase_name, constituent_array,
                      site_ratios):
        """
        Return an abstract syntax tree of the mole fraction of the
        given species as a function of its constituent site fractions.

        Note that this will treat vacancies the same as any other component,
        i.e., this will not give the correct _overall_ composition for
        sublattices containing vacancies with other components by normalizing
        by a factor of 1 - y_{VA}. This is because we use this routine in the
        order-disorder model to calculate the disordered site fractions from
        the ordered site fractions, so we need _all_ site fractions, including
        VA, to sum to unity.
        """

        # Normalize site ratios
        site_ratio_normalization = 0
        numerator = S.Zero
        for idx, sublattice in enumerate(constituent_array):
            # sublattices with only vacancies don't count
            if sum(spec.number_of_atoms for spec in list(sublattice)) == 0:
                continue
            if species_name in list(sublattice):
                site_ratio_normalization += site_ratios[idx]
                numerator += site_ratios[idx] * \
                    v.SiteFraction(phase_name, idx, species_name)

        if site_ratio_normalization == 0 and species_name.name == 'VA':
            return 1

        if site_ratio_normalization == 0:
            raise ValueError('Couldn\'t find ' + species_name + ' in ' + \
                str(constituent_array))

        return numerator / site_ratio_normalization

    @staticmethod
    def _partitioned_sublattice_groups(ordered_constituents, disordered_constituents):
        """
        Return the ordered sublattices corresponding to each disordered sublattice.

        In a partitioned (order-disorder) model, the ordered phase description
        splits sublattices of the disordered description into several
        symmetry-distinct position classes of the same physical lattice. Every
        sublattice of the disordered description therefore corresponds to a
        group of one or more sublattices of the ordered description. Sublattices
        that are not split by the ordered description (e.g. interstitial or
        vacancy-only sublattices) correspond to a group of exactly one ordered
        sublattice, and their occupancies are unaffected by ordering.

        Following the convention of thermodynamic databases (and of the site
        ratios declared by both descriptions), the sublattices created by the
        ordering split are the leading sublattices of the ordered description,
        while the trailing sublattices correspond one-to-one to the trailing
        sublattices of the disordered description.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ordered_constituents : list of list of Species
            Constituents of every sublattice of the ordered description.
        disordered_constituents : list of list of Species
            Constituents of every sublattice of the disordered description.

        Returns
        -------
        list of tuple of int
            For each sublattice of the disordered description, the indices of
            the corresponding sublattices of the ordered description.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> # (AL,FE)(AL,FE)(AL,FE)(AL,FE)(VA) ordering of (AL,FE)(VA)
        >>> Model._partitioned_sublattice_groups([['AL', 'FE']]*4 + [['VA']], [['AL', 'FE'], ['VA']])
        [(0, 1, 2, 3), (4,)]
        """
        num_ordered_subl = len(ordered_constituents)
        num_disordered_subl = len(disordered_constituents)

"""Stronger, randomized verification that the partitioned (order-disorder) model
reduces exactly to the disordered model at every disordered configuration."""
import sys, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/task/source')
import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Database, Model, variables as v

def max_abs_dev(dbf, ordered, comps, n_trials=25, seed=0):
    dis = dbf.phases[ordered].model_hints['disordered_phase']
    mo, md = Model(dbf, comps, ordered), Model(dbf, comps, dis)
    groups = Model._partitioned_sublattice_groups(dbf.phases[ordered].constituents,
                                                  dbf.phases[dis].constituents)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    go = mo.GM
    gd = md.GM
    worst = 0.0
    for trial in range(n_trials):
        T = float(rng.uniform(300., 2000.))
        base = {v.T: T, v.P: 101325.0, v.N: 1.0}
        so, sd = dict(base), dict(base)
        for di, group in enumerate(groups):
            # a single random disordered occupancy for the whole group / disordered sublattice
            species = sorted(set(md.constituents[di]) | set().union(*[set(mo.constituents[i]) for i in group]))
            w = rng.random(len(species)) + 1e-3
            w /= w.sum()
            occ = dict(zip(species, w))
            for sp in md.constituents[di]:
                sd[v.SiteFraction(dis, di, sp)] = occ[sp]
            for i in group:
                # renormalize over the species actually present in this ordered sublattice
                tot = sum(occ[sp] for sp in mo.constituents[i])
                for sp in mo.constituents[i]:
                    so[v.SiteFraction(ordered, i, sp)] = occ[sp] / tot
        dev = abs(float(go.subs(so).n(50)) - float(gd.subs(sd).n(50)))
        scale = max(abs(float(gd.subs(sd).n(50))), 1.0)
        worst = max(worst, dev/scale)
    return worst

alfe = Database('/workspace/task/fixtures/al_fe_c_benchmark.tdb')
alni = Database('/workspace/task/source/examples/NI_AL_DUPIN_2001.TDB')
sei = Database('/workspace/task/source/examples/alfe_sei.TDB')
cases = [(alfe, 'BCC_4SL', ['AL','FE','VA']), (alfe, 'BCC_NOB', ['AL','FE','VA']),
         (alfe, 'BCC_VA', ['AL','FE','VA']), (alfe, 'B2_BCC', ['AL','FE','VA']),
         (alfe, 'FCC_4SL', ['AL','FE','VA']), (alfe, 'BCC_R2', ['AL','FE','VA']),
         (alfe, 'BCC_R2', ['AL','FE','C','VA']), (alfe, 'BCC_4SL', ['AL','VA']),
         (alfe, 'BCC_4SL', ['FE','VA']),
         (alni, 'BCC_B2', ['AL','NI','VA']), (alni, 'FCC_L12', ['AL','NI','VA']),
         (alni, 'FCC_L12', ['AL','VA']), (sei, 'B2_BCC', ['AL','FE','VA'])]
ok = True
for dbf, ph, comps in cases:
    try:
        w = max_abs_dev(dbf, ph, comps)
    except Exception as e:
        print('%-9s %-16s FAILED %s: %s' % (ph, ','.join(comps), type(e).__name__, e)); ok = False; continue
    flag = 'OK ' if w < 1e-12 else 'BAD'
    if w >= 1e-12: ok = False
    print('%s %-9s %-16s max relative deviation = %.3e' % (flag, ph, ','.join(comps), w))
print('ALL CONSISTENT' if ok else 'INCONSISTENCIES FOUND')
EOF

"""Generality checks on a synthetic database with interstitial ordering."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/task/source')
import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Database, Model, calculate, equilibrium, variables as v

dbf = Database('/workspace/task/scratch/synthetic_ord.tdb')

def reduction_check(ordered, comps, n_trials=20, seed=1):
    dis = dbf.phases[ordered].model_hints['disordered_phase']
    mo, md = Model(dbf, comps, ordered), Model(dbf, comps, dis)
    groups = Model._partitioned_sublattice_groups(dbf.phases[ordered].constituents,
                                                  dbf.phases[dis].constituents)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    worst = 0.0
    for _ in range(n_trials):
        T = float(rng.uniform(300., 1500.))
        so = {v.T: T, v.P: 101325.0, v.N: 1.0}
        sd = dict(so)
        for di, group in enumerate(groups):
            species = sorted(set(md.constituents[di]))
            w = rng.random(len(species)) + 1e-3
            w /= w.sum()
            occ = dict(zip(species, w))
            for sp in md.constituents[di]:
                sd[v.SiteFraction(dis, di, sp)] = occ[sp]
            for i in group:
                tot = sum(occ[sp] for sp in mo.constituents[i])
                for sp in mo.constituents[i]:
                    so[v.SiteFraction(ordered, i, sp)] = occ[sp] / tot
        go = float(mo.GM.subs(so).n(50)); gd = float(md.GM.subs(sd).n(50))
        worst = max(worst, abs(go - gd) / max(abs(gd), 1.0))
    print('  reduction %-6s %-12s groups=%-18s max rel dev = %.3e  %s'
          % (ordered, ','.join(comps), groups, worst, 'OK' if worst < 1e-12 else '*** BAD ***'))
    return worst

print('== partitioned model reduces to disordered model at disordered configurations')
worst = 0.0
for ordered, comps in [('FCC_O', ['AA','BB','CC','VA']), ('FCC_O', ['AA','BB','VA']),
                       ('BCC_O', ['AA','BB','CC','VA']), ('BCC_O', ['AA','BB','VA']),
                       ('HCP_O', ['AA','BB']), ('FCC_O', ['AA','CC','VA'])]:
    worst = max(worst, reduction_check(ordered, comps))

print('== global sampling: partitioned phase never above its disordered counterpart')
for ordered, comps in [('FCC_O', ['AA','BB','CC','VA']), ('FCC_O', ['AA','BB','VA']),
                       ('BCC_O', ['AA','BB','CC','VA']), ('HCP_O', ['AA','BB'])]:
    dis = dbf.phases[ordered].model_hints['disordered_phase']
    for T in (400., 900.):
        co = calculate(dbf, comps, ordered, T=T, P=101325, pdens=2000)
        cd = calculate(dbf, comps, dis, T=T, P=101325, pdens=2000)
        # compare convex-hull-like minimum energy at matched compositions (binned)
        el = [c for c in sorted(comps) if c != 'VA'][0]
        xo = co.X.sel(component=el).values.squeeze(); go = co.GM.values.squeeze()
        xd = cd.X.sel(component=el).values.squeeze(); gd = cd.GM.values.squeeze()
        bins = np.linspace(0, 1, 21)
        io = np.digitize(xo, bins); id_ = np.digitize(xd, bins)
        bad = 0
        for b in range(1, len(bins) + 1):
            mo_, md_ = go[io == b], gd[id_ == b]
            if len(mo_) and len(md_) and mo_.min() > md_.min() + 1e-6*max(1, abs(md_.min())):
                bad += 1
        print('  %-6s %-12s T=%6.1f bins with ordered > disordered: %d' % (ordered, ','.join(comps), T, bad))
print('worst reduction deviation:', worst)
EOF

The repair is complete and verified.

## Common cause

`Model.atomic_ordering_energy` (`source/pycalphad/model.py`) implements the partitioned order–disorder model

```
G(y) = G_dis(x(y)) + [ G_ord(y) − G_ord(x(y)) ]
```

which needs the correspondence between the ordered description's sublattices and the disordered description's sublattices. That correspondence was guessed with a heuristic: a sublattice was treated as "not created by the ordering split" only if the *species was VA* **and** the *database declared exactly one constituent* for it (plus the assumption "pure vacancy sublattices are always last"); everything else was mapped by *species membership* through `mole_fraction`.

So for any phase where a non-ordering sublattice declares more than one constituent — an interstitial `(C,VA)` sublattice, notably when C is not among the requested components — the interstitial occupancy was aggregated with the substitutional position classes that share the species VA:

* `Y(BCC_R1,1,VA)` → `0.5·Y(BCC_R2,0,VA) + 0.5·Y(BCC_R2,1,VA)` (≈ 0) instead of `Y(BCC_R2,2,VA)` (= 1), and the ordered `Y(BCC_R2,2,VA)` was replaced instead of left alone.

Consequence: the ordering term did not vanish at a disordered configuration (−46 697 J/mol for `BCC_R2`/`BCC_R1` with AL–FE–VA; +13 526 J/mol with C added), so a redundant representation of a phase already in the assessment became artificially stable (NP = 0.147, ΔGM = −1336 J/mol, ΔMU ≈ ±19 000 J/mol) — one defect producing all four symptoms.

## Fix

The mapping is now derived structurally, not from a species/constituent-count heuristic (two private helpers plus rewritten substitution loops; `Model.mole_fraction` and all public APIs untouched):

* `_partitioned_sublattice_groups`: the leading `n_ord − n_dis + 1` ordered sublattices are the position classes partitioning the first disordered sublattice; remaining sublattices map one-to-one (raises `DofError` if the disordered description has more sublattices).
* `_disordered_site_fraction`: for a partitioned group, the site-ratio-weighted average over the group (guaranteeing occupancies sum to 1); for a one-sublattice group, the site fraction itself — interstitials and vacancy-only sublattices are never mixed with the ordering lattice, whatever their position.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Ordering term at disordered configurations, all pairs in both databases (25 randomized T/composition trials each) | max rel. deviation ≤ 5×10⁻¹⁵ (was 0.15–0.72 for `BCC_R2`) |
| Model ASTs vs. pre-fix baseline, 13 phases incl. `BCC_4SL`, `B2_BCC`, `BCC_VA`, `FCC_4SL`, `FCC_L12` (0.75/0.25), `BCC_B2` | byte-identical (0 differing) |
| Equilibrium with vs. without the redundant `BCC_R1`/`BCC_R2`, (T, X) grid 900–1500 K × 0.05–0.95 | max \|ΔGM\| = 0, \|ΔMU\| = 0, \|ΔNP\| = 0, identical assemblages (baseline: solver crash / spurious phase) |
| Documented references in `docs/examples/EquilibriumWithOrdering.rst` | CP 25.4496/26.9323/28.4724/30.1806/32.1556 (docs 25.45…32.16), GM/MU/DOO match; Al–Ni `FCC_L12` NP 0.63614/0.36386 (docs 0.6363/0.3637), γ′ vanishes ≈750 K |
| Generality on synthetic databases (5→2 sublattice ordering with `(C,VA)` interstitial; 4→3 with VA-only sublattice *before* the interstitial; 2→1 with 0.6/0.4 ratios; magnetic TC mapping) | all reduce exactly; partitioned GM ≤ disordered GM (baseline failed 4 of these) |
| Unrelated databases (`alzn_mey`, `nbre_liu`, `Al-Mg_Zhong`), `calculate`, HM/SM/CPM/DOO/TC | unaffected |
| `python reproduce.py` | exit 0, `workflow_completed`, 9 points per study |
